baseline.bindingConstraint: AUTHOR CAPACITY — human time to write EW, not infrastructure

agent_h_integration_design.title: 300→600→800 Integration Architecture

pipeline.description: Strictly acyclic three-stage pipeline. Each stage consumes upstream outputs, never produces them. 300 is read-only; 600 is authoring-only; 800 certifies and writes.
pipeline.acyclicVerification: CONFIRMED — no reverse edges, no circular ownership, no chicken-and-egg

300_to_600.signal: Composite 0-100 score per item across 6 dimensions
300_to_600.useBy600: Rank items by quality deficit. Author EW starting with lowest-UIQS items. Target grade C/D/F items (1,299 items at UIQS <70) for EW enrichment.

300_to_600.signal: EW fill rate, distractor overlap %, non-discriminating distractor count, duplicate-distractor pairs
300_to_600.useBy600: Identify items where distractors are identical/near-identical (DL-005 findings). Target items with 100% identical distractor pairs first. Select distractor patterns for template library.

300_to_600.signal: EC length, EC content richness (references, formula, trap), rewrite candidate flag, learning value score
300_to_600.useBy600: Flag items with EC < 100 chars for EC expansion. Flag items with no ASC/COSO reference (EV3 violation). Cert-reject items with EC < 50 chars.
300_to_600.priorityWeight: Medium — EC quality gap, not safety-critical

300_to_600.signal: Domain alignment, section alignment, LOS mapping completeness, blueprint coverage gaps
300_to_600.useBy600: Identify blueprint gaps for new-item authoring (Domain F 149 greenfield items). Prioritize undersampled LOS areas.
300_to_600.priorityWeight: Medium — guides greenfield authoring, not existing-item repair

300_to_600.signal: Case-bank exhibit quality, cognitive load audit, learning friction register, exhibit dependency audit
300_to_600.useBy600: Target case items with missing exhibit references or decorative data. Build EW templates for case-bank items (310 items at 3.9% EW fill).

300_to_600.signal: 46 P0 items (immediate learner-safety risk), 583 P1 items (high priority), remaining P2 (medium/low)
300_to_600.useBy600: Strict priority queue: P0 items author EW first (within 2 sessions), then P1, then P2. P0 items with EW debt get factory-pipeline priority.
300_to_600.priorityWeight: Critical — blocks certification and learner safety

600_to_800.description: Item with all 3 non-CC ExplanationWrong slots filled with choice-specific text (≥50 chars, no boilerplate, references domain concept), ExplanationCorrect ≥150 chars with principle reference, metadata complete per QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md
600_to_800.preCertQAGate: Automated: DL-008 scan (EW[CC] empty), EW non-empty check (all 3 non-CC slots), EW uniqueness check (no identical EW across slots), EW minimum-length check (≥50 chars), boilerplate detection (DL-013 pattern scan), EC length audit, parse validity, certified count stability
600_to_800.passCriterion: All pre-cert QA gates PASS before handoff to 800. Items failing any gate return to 600 for re-author.

300_to_800.status: ALREADY OPERATIONAL — S802/S803 use S302-S309 analytics for certification priority. No new integration needed.
300_to_800.gap: None. 300→800 data flow is complete and proven.

rejectionFeedbackLoop.description: 800 rejects → 600 re-authors → re-submits through pre-cert QA gate
rejectionFeedbackLoop.expectedRejectionRate: 5-10% for first-wave items, 2-5% for subsequent waves
rejectionReasons: CAQS §1.6 audit fails (correctness, precision, difficulty, distractor, blueprint, relevance)
Pre-cert QA gate fails (structural: EW empty, duplicate, too short)
rejectionFeedbackLoop.mitigation: Pre-cert QA gate catches structural issues before 800 human review, reducing rejection rate. Content issues (CAQS §1.6) can only be caught at 800.

edges.type: Content — pre-authored items delivered for certification
Rejection — items fail certification, return for re-author
edges.cycleRisk: None — this is a feedback loop, not a dependency cycle. Same item re-enters 600, gets re-authored, re-enters 800. No analytics flow backward.

circularDependencyCheck.boundaryEnforcement: 300 reads pack files, never writes. 600 writes ExplanationWrong/ExplanationCorrect fields, never produces analytics. 800 writes question_state and certifies. No stage can perform another stage's function.
circularDependencyCheck.chickenEggGaps: None. All 300-series analytics (S302-S306) already exist and are complete. 600 would have full analytic coverage from Day 1. No analytic gap to fill before 600 can begin.

agent_h_integration_design.recommendation: Integration architecture is sound on paper: acyclic, well-defined handoffs, clear QA gates. However, it DOES NOT resolve the binding constraint (author capacity) — the pipeline is a handoff mechanism, not a capacity multiplier. DEFER consistent with S309 analysis.

domainCompletionTimeline.domainF: Sessions 5-11 (7 sessions — 149 greenfield items, partially parallel with E after session 5)

totalSessionsTo100pct.conservativeExplanation: If 600 infrastructure takes longer to stabilize (5 sessions startup), and parallel overhead from three-lane execution adds 2 sessions: 5 + (14+2) = 21. With moderate rework: 24.

ewFillAtCompletion.mcq: ~92% — factory model reaches more items per session, potential to close additional ~200 slots
ewFillAtCompletion.caseBank: ~85% — factory pipeline can sustain higher velocity for case-bank items
ewFillAtCompletion.remainingGap: ~500 slots — smaller than Option A due to higher EW throughput

domainCompletionTimeline.domainE_600PreAuthored: 600 authors EW for 167 Domain E items during sessions 1-5 (parallel with cert waves)
domainCompletionTimeline.domainF_600PreAuthored: 600 authors EW for 149 Domain F items during sessions 4-8 (parallel)
domainCompletionTimeline.domainE_cert: Sessions 5-11 (7 sessions — EW already authored, cert-only)
domainCompletionTimeline.domainF_cert: Sessions 7-13 (7 sessions — parallel with E after methodology baseline)

agent_i_throughput_model.conclusion: Option A (No 600-series) is the Pareto-optimal choice. Option B adds 1 session (+5.9%) to certification timeline, adds governance complexity (+50%), introduces handoff rework risk, and only improves EW fill by 4-5%. The binding constraint (AUTHOR CAPACITY) is not addressed by infrastructure — tools cannot write explanations. S309's DEFER recommendation is confirmed.

agent_n_dependency_review.title: Dependency Chain Validation — 300 / 600 / 800 Series
agent_n_dependency_review.methodology: Dependency-graph analysis with cycle detection, ownership boundary verification, and chicken-and-egg gap audit. Validated against AGENTS.md §2 (read-only by default), PROJECT_CONSTITUTION.md, and COLLABORATION_MATRIX.md.

300_series.description: Read-only analytics pipeline (S302-S310). Produces DQS, EQS, BQS, ExQS, UIQS models.

600_series.description: Content authoring infrastructure. Produces pre-authored EW/EC content, QA-gated certification candidates.

800_series.description: Certification pipeline. Certifies items via CAQS §1.6 six-dimension audit.

edges.description: DQS/EQS/BQS/ExQS/UIQS models inform 600's authoring priority queue. 600 never produces analytics consumed by 300.
edges.status: READY — all S302-S306 analytics exist. 600 would receive complete coverage from Day 1.

edges.description: Pre-authored items with QA-gated EW/EC delivered for certification. 800 certifies; 800 never authors into 600.
edges.status: DESIGN — handoff protocol defined (pre-cert QA gate). No existing implementation.

edges.description: UIQS rankings, P0/P1 risk flags, bottleneck analysis inform 800's certification priority. Already operational per S802/S803.
edges.status: OPERATIONAL — S802 consumed S302-S306 analytics for Wave 1 priority.

edges.description: Items failing CAQS §1.6 audit return to 600 for re-author. This is a content-loop, not a dependency — 600 does not depend on 800 rejecting items to function.
edges.status: DESIGN — rejection protocol defined. ~5-10% expected rejection rate.

rules.rule: No stage can perform another stage's exclusive function

rules.status: VERIFIED — certification authority is sole at 800
VERIFIED — answer-key authority is sole at 800 (per DL-030 precedent)

scenariosChecked.scenario: 600 needs analytics to prioritize, but 300 hasn't produced them yet
scenariosChecked.status: NOT A GAP — all S302-S306 analytics are complete and available. UIQS, DQS, EQS, BQS, ExQS models exist for all 2,500 MCQ and 400 case items. 600 would start with full analytic coverage.

scenariosChecked.scenario: 800 needs pre-authored EW from 600, but 600 hasn't built infrastructure yet
scenariosChecked.status: NOT A GAP — this is the 600 startup cost (4 sessions), not a circular dependency. 800 can still certify items without pre-authored EW (current model). 600 output is additive, not prerequisite.

scenariosChecked.scenario: 300 needs 600-authored items for analytics, but 600 hasn't produced any yet
scenariosChecked.status: NOT A GAP — 300 operates on existing pack-file content, not 600 output. No reverse dependency exists.

scenariosChecked.scenario: 600 needs 800 certification to know which items to author for
scenariosChecked.status: NOT A GAP — 300's analytics already identify which items need EW authoring regardless of certification state. The UIQS P0/P1 priority queue is independent of certification.

circularOwnershipCheck.graphVerification: Directed acyclic graph confirmed. Edges: 300→600, 600→800, 300→800, 800→600 (conditional rejection only, not ownership). No path creates a cycle because: (1) 300 never writes to pack files, (2) 600 never writes to analytics, (3) 800 never writes to analytics or EW fields. The 800→600 rejection edge returns the SAME item for re-author, not a new dependency. Re-entry does not create a cycle — it's linear re-processing of a single item.

agent_n_dependency_review.conclusion: Dependency architecture is sound — acyclic, well-bounded, no gaps. The integration model works on paper. However, sound architecture does not equal net benefit. The DEFER recommendation stands because architecture quality does not overcome the near-zero throughput gain.

agent_q_roadmap_adjustment.title: Roadmap Adjustment Analysis — If 600-Series Launches
agent_q_roadmap_adjustment.baselinePlan: S309 execution plan: 17 sessions expected (14-22 range). Tracks: 300 closeout → Domain E/F cert + Case-bank EW → Pack A closeout → Governance closure. Modernization deferred to post-cert (10 sessions).

changesToS803PlusCertificationWaves.speedChange: MARGINALLY FASTER — pre-authored EW removes the EW-authoring phase from certification sessions. Cert reviewers only perform CAQS §1.6 audit, not EW authoring.

quantification.certSessionDuration: Reduced from ~18 items/session (cert + EW) to ~15 items/session (cert-only, but without EW blocking)
quantification.netEffect: Certification sessions become ~20% faster in wall-clock per session, but cert velocity (items/session) is unchanged because CAQS §1.6 audit per item is invariant.
quantification.sessionsSaved: 2-3 sessions saved from 800-series (EW pre-authored, no authoring bottleneck in cert sessions).

changesToS803PlusCertificationWaves.risk: Pre-authored EW may not match cert reviewer's expectations — handoff rework risk. CAQS §1.6 audit is unchanged; certification quality is unchanged.

dl013Boilerplate.status: DEFERRED (no change) — DL-013 ~851 fields remain deferred to post-cert in both scenarios. 600 does not accelerate DL-013 because boilerplate removal is batch find-replace, not explanation authoring.
dl013Boilerplate.acceleration: None. DL-013 and 600 address different defect categories.

dl031DifficultyInflation.status: DEFERRED (no change) — DL-031 ~500 items remain deferred. Difficulty recalibration requires per-item cognitive assessment, not EW authoring.

dl032CaseCalibration.status: DEFERRED (no change) — Case-bank uniform Moderate labeling is pedagogical, not safety-critical.

ecNormalization.status: DEFERRED (no change) — Cross-pack EC normalization is quality polish.

changesToModernizationRoadmap.netEffect: Zero modernization acceleration. 600 addresses EW authoring (distractor explanations), not modernization (boilerplate removal, difficulty calibration, EC normalization). Different defect domains.

changesToEWRoadmap.description: 2,403-slot gap (per S307: case-bank EW at 3.9% fill, MCQ EW debt of 539 items). 600 factory model could accelerate EW production.

acceleration.ewVelocity: 39 → 50 items/session (28% improvement per S309 EW Factory Model Agent O)

gapClosureTimeline.without600: ~18 sessions to fill 2,403 slots at 39 items/session (including cert-embedded authoring)
gapClosureTimeline.with600: ~14 sessions to fill 2,403 slots at 50 items/session (dedicated factory pipeline)

acceleration.caveat: EW authoring is NOT on the critical path. The critical path is certification (CAQS §1.6 audit). Faster EW authoring doesn't accelerate certification completion because cert reviewers cannot review faster than ~15 items/session regardless of EW readiness. The EW gap closure is a parallel track, not critical-path work.

changesToEWRoadmap.largestImpact: Case-bank EW (310 items at 3.9% fill). Dedicated factory pipeline could close this in ~6 sessions (50 items/session) vs. ~8 sessions (39 items/session).

changesToS309ExecutionPlan.s309Plan: 17 sessions expected (14-22 range). Tracks: 300 closeout (2) → Domain E/F cert + EW (10) → Pack A closeout (3) → Governance (2).

with600.startup: Add 4 sessions at beginning for 600 infrastructure build + pilot
with600.certPhase: Reduce by 3 sessions (EW pre-authored removes inline authoring)

criticalPathChange.before: 300 closeout → Domain E/F cert → Pack A closeout → Governance
criticalPathChange.after: 300 closeout → 600 startup (4 sessions) → Domain E/F cert (with pre-authored EW) → Pack A closeout → Governance
criticalPathChange.criticalPathElongated: 4 sessions added to critical path during startup phase. Reduced by 3 during cert phase. Net: +1 session on critical path.

agent_q_roadmap_adjustment.conclusion: 600-series activation would not accelerate the portfolio roadmap. It adds 4 sessions of startup to the critical path, saves 2-3 sessions during certification, nets +1-3 sessions worse. Modernization is unaffected (different defect domains). EW gap closes ~4 sessions faster but EW is not on the critical path. S309's DEFER recommendation is confirmed.

agent_r_session_reduction.title: Session Reduction Forecast — S308 Baseline vs. S309 Optimized vs. 600-Enabled
agent_r_session_reduction.methodology: S308 forecast engine baseline (30 sessions). S309 expected scenario (17 sessions). 600-overlay from S309_600_SERIES_FEASIBILITY.json and agent_i_throughput_model above.

s308_baseline.description: Original 7-phase forecast: 300 closeout → DL-008 remediation → Structural remediation → Domain E/F cert → Pack A closeout → Calibration → Governance. Included DL-008 (3 sessions), modernization (10 sessions), sequential E→F execution.
s308_baseline.status: SUPERSEDED by S309 — contains DL-008 false positive, includes deferred modernization

s309_optimistic.description: Best-case: all levers confirmed, 3-track parallel, sustained 15 items/session, no rework, replace-vs-repair + factory model boost.

s309_expected.description: Realistic: DL-008 removed, modernization deferred, E/F partially parallelized, governance batched. Standard execution cadence.

s309_conservative.description: Safe: DL-008 removed, modernization deferred. No parallelization. Sequential E then F.
s309_conservative.status: FLOOR — achievable with simple sequential execution

with600_optimistic.description: 600 pre-authors EW for all cert-blocked items. Factory model at maximum velocity (50 items/session). Startup compressed to 3 sessions. Zero handoff rework. All parallel tracks successful.
with600_optimistic.status: STRETCH — requires 600 startup compression + maximum velocity + zero rework. Achievable only if 600 outperforms its projected savings.

with600_expected.description: 600 startup (4 sessions) + cert with pre-authored EW (14 sessions). Factory model at 50 items/session. Standard handoff overhead. Some rework from cert/author misalignment.
with600_expected.status: WORSE THAN S309 — 600 costs more than it saves

with600_conservative.description: 600 startup (5 sessions) + cert (16 sessions). Factory model at 39 items/session (no throughput gain). Handoff rework adds 2-3 sessions. Parallel overhead from 3-lane coordination.
with600_conservative.status: SIGNIFICANTLY WORSE — infrastructure overhead overwhelms savings

s309Only.appliesTo: S309, partially to 600-enabled (+1 from batch, -1 from 3-lane overhead)

600Specific.lever: EW pre-authoring removes inline EW from cert sessions

600Specific.status: MEDIUM — 39→50 items/session is 28% improvement but EW is not critical path

netSessionDifference.expectedOutcome: 600 adds 1 session to the certification timeline with ±3 session variance depending on execution quality. Range: -2 (optimistic) to +7 (conservative). Central estimate: +1 (slightly worse than S309).

whenDoes600BecomeBeneficial.breakevenCondition: If 600 startup cost ≤ 2 sessions AND EW factory velocity ≥ 60 items/session AND 600→800 handoff rework rate ≤ 2%
whenDoes600BecomeBeneficial.currentFeasibility: NONE of these conditions are met. Startup is 4 sessions. Factory velocity upper bound is ~50 items/session. Rejection rate is 5-10% per historical patterns.
triggerForReevaluation: EW authoring becomes the binding constraint on certification throughput (currently: certification audit is the constraint, not EW)
Portfolio grows to 5,000+ items making dedicated authoring infrastructure cost-effective
Observed cert velocity drops below 10 items/session due to EW-blocked items
Post-S309 execution shows EW authoring is the actual bottleneck (not just predicted)

agent_r_session_reduction.conclusion: S309's 17-session expected forecast is the best available estimate. Adding 600-series infrastructure changes that to 18 sessions expected (range 15-24). The expected case is WORSE by 1 session. The optimistic case saves 2 sessions. The conservative case adds 7 sessions. Expected value analysis: DEFER 600-series. The 300→800 direct path (S309 model) is the optimal execution strategy.

consolidated_recommendation.basis: Five-agent independent analysis (H, I, N, Q, R) converges on the same conclusion as S309 single-agent K: the 600-series adds a handoff layer without resolving the binding constraint (author capacity). Integration architecture is sound on paper (Agent H/N) but net throughput impact is -1 to +1 sessions (Agent I/R). Modernization roadmap is unaffected (Agent Q). S309's 17-session expected plan remains the optimal path.
consolidated_recommendation.recommendedAction: Proceed with S310 (Portfolio Operations Dashboard — 300-series final session). Execute S309's 17-session plan without 600-series. Re-evaluate 600-series feasibility after 800-series Waves 2-3 if authoring velocity empirically proves to be the bottleneck.
